Track: Coordination

## C1118 — P post-PR local capacity & evidence-retention policy: CONDITIONAL ADOPT (Release-first, verified-restore-before-delete)

**Authority / goal.** Work-start Compass → Product/Value Strategy §1.1 and §1.3 → Development Process §§3(P/T),4.1.2–4.1.3,4.3.1–4.3.2/7 → main CURRENT_SPEC; storage is operational, NOT semantic/Product authority. Adopt as the **default housekeeping policy for future P work** the user's two intentions: (1) archive genuinely necessary, non-reconstructible original evidence off the Codex Cloud work disk, preferring GitHub Release assets when permitted; (2) delete old P-owned local copies and regenerable build/cache material not needed for current PR repair or next authorized task. This is **conditional** on verified retention and restore, not carte-blanche `rm -rf` and not permission to erase private F/R evidence, shared toolchains, active worktrees or unreleased Git commits.

**Actual verified pilot.** User's [2026-11-17 P Codex report](https://github.com/wakairo/NewLang_Compiler/issues/1496#issuecomment-6947423473) claims `NEWLANG_RELEASE_PAT` used to upload 34-byte synthetic `newlang-machine-pilot.txt`, HTTP 201, same-agent download `cmp` and SHA256 `63a9fed47b4cde5eedc848584e7f33d7076f61bca05b11d9f64d880c1d7f407d`. C independently GitHub API GET-verified Release **448433010**, `draft=true`, `published_at=null`, tag request `archive-upload-pilot-20261117`, existing uploaded Asset **758861590**, size34, GitHub-declared digest identical. **Fresh, separate Codex task GET/sha256 of that very asset is NOT_RUN**. The previous [AUTHORIZATION_BLOCKED with inherited credentials](https://github.com/wakairo/NewLang_Compiler/issues/1496#issuecomment-6944827944) is historical and not retroactive PASS; the successful explicit token path is distinct. Current Release storage path is plausible, not yet accepted as sole durable storage for any real irreplaceable evidence. Do NOT publish the draft as a software release, expose any confidential raw/creds, or assume the draft is a secret vault.

### Operational P default (one short checkpoint, not a new compiler CI gate)
1. **At each DRAFT PR publication (and earlier whenever disk/inode demand warrants):** classify the P-owned workspace into (A) remote-tracked, reachable *published Git commits/refs* and reviewable source/tests/oracles, (B) original unique FIRST/RED, exact run logs/status, measured outputs/ELFs/configs and forward/private history not yet recoverable from Git, (C) reproducible rebuild objects, temporary download/packaging duplicates, obsolete worktrees/caches, and (D) active HEAD/worktree, pending PR repair inputs, single needed pinned SDK and next-work reusable artifacts. **Do not treat reproducible rerun as recovering a historical original observation.** Any uncommitted/unpushed/ref-unreachable Git state is NOT category A until preserved (safe branch/ref or verified Git bundle). P alone determines whether an item is genuinely needed for candidate repair; keep F/R independent custody untouched.
2. **Archive necessary unique B**, only if nonsecret/authorized for eventual public release visibility, using bounded archive(s) rather than one huge file tree. Include originals, metadata/stage and status (FIRST/RED/NOT_RUN not changed into PASS), clear member manifest (path/size/SHA), immutable source/main/base/PR HEAD/tree, and asset SHA/size. Preserve minimum original Git/bundle objects in Git as appropriate; **do not commit huge binary archives to normal main**. Use dedicated evidence **DRAFT Release** (current pilot remains DRAFT, don't publish automatically), unique non-overwriting asset names identifying P/Issue/HEAD and preferably SHA; uploading is not evidence of independent restoration. Respect ≤2GiB/asset and Release limitations; evaluate a new destination if exceeded. Avoid archiving `.git` credentials, environment variables, tokens, private F/R originals, private configs, symlinks pointing out of the allowlisted workspace or malicious extraction paths.
3. **Deletion gate = verified remote recoverability:** on each actual evidence archive, finish remote upload → GET Release+asset ID/length/digest metadata → **download actual full bytes via authenticated separate clean destination** → compare expected size and SHA256 → verify every necessary member + safe restore and Git-bundle prerequisites → record short durable Issue/Git receipt with URL/id/size/hash, original HEAD/status and restore outcome. Before **first destructive P migration to Releases**, independently confirm the already-uploaded pilot asset from a **new Codex task/session** using a correctly scoped read credential, then perform the same complete restore proof for the first real P archive. On mismatch, auth/restore failure or unverified private material, retain originals and STOP affected deletion; existing independently restored Git/LFS archive remains unchanged until **each** old asset is individually migrated and fresh-restored. No automatic deleting of Release assets; release assets are editable/deletable and GitHub alone isn't immutable or a guaranteed forever backup. Extra copy of unusually critical independent originals may be warranted.
4. **Delete aggressively after gate:** safe P-owned, explicitly identified old local evidence/archive-upload/download caches, unnecessary compiled objects and finished redundant sanitizer matrix workdirs; retain **only** active PR/repair worktree, needed current source/commit, one shared pinned toolchain/SDK and assets truly reused next task. Do not touch files of F/R/T, other running agents or shared service caches without ownership/need confirmation. Do not delete before completed work is published, nor assume PR publication alone preserves unpushed work. Avoid broad recursive deletion outside confirmed P-owned paths. P's routine bounded cleanup is autonomous under Process §4.1.2; no C micro-release per file.
5. **Capacity prevention is continuous, not just post-PR:** before each large sanitizer/full build, and after major generation, inspect **both available bytes and inodes**, predicted peak temporary duplicate/ELF/build footprint plus safety margin. The prior ~7.8GiB disk with >3GiB sanitizer peaks/actual byte and inode exhaustion makes a fixed 4GiB free threshold unreliable. P may schedule matrix serially/clean regenerable intermediates after evidence preservation and select low-cost tooling; no skipping any required negative/native/sanitizer/OOM checks. If predicted run cannot fit, stop **that build**, free safe reproducibles/reassess or return to C for environment/scope resource decision rather than repeatedly ENOSPC and treating run as PASS. Report a compact receipt (remote archive/restore status, removed approximate bytes/inodes, remaining free bytes/inodes, next-build estimate) once per meaningful checkpoint, not a new yearly manifest protocol.

**Adoption/next action.** C ACCEPTS **Release-first as the default for eligible P-generated large unique evidence** and **verified-post-PR minimal local retention** as operational policy, conditional on the first fresh-agent pilot restore and per-archive validation above. Does not mandate Releases for unpublished/private or oversized data; ordinary Git/bundle for original source, current proven Git/LFS as fallback, R2/B2 deferred. Does not immediately authorize historic mass migration, old verified LFS deletion, broad disk wipe, publication, account/credential edits or new compiler/CI/PR/merge work. One bounded **read-only new-Codex-session** retrieval of pilot Asset 758861590 (expected 34B / SHA above) is the remaining first-mile verification; report back on this Issue. Then future P may execute scoped housekeeping on its own verified data without recurring C micro-GO. This storage checkpoint is not a new PR1495/main merge gate or Product GO. Product GO #624 PAUSED / H1 #268 HOLD.

**Stop / owner.** Material provenance/source loss, original FIRST/RED corruption, missing remote authenticated restore, unsafe public disclosure, repo/production/CI/PR modification, unknown P/F/R ownership, changing live work or exceeding budget => affected deletion STOP, preserve source and notify C. P captain handles its own local inventory and operation; C rules policy/safety limits, T may advise but is not a mandatory signoff. Goal is near-minimal **verified recoverable** Codex disk footprint with adequate byte+inode reserve, **not** a claim of infinite disk space.
